objectives.title: Read the flag
objectives.prompt: With only a username list, AS-REP roast the account whose Kerberos pre-authentication is disabled, crack its AS-REP hash offline to recover the password, then read flag.txt from the //dc/imaging share that only that account may open.
hints: The real-world technique needs no credentials, only usernames: an account with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled makes the KDC return an AS-REP to an unauthenticated request. Point your resolver and /etc/krb5.conf at the DC, then roast the list: GetNPUsers.py LAKESIDE.LAB/ -usersfile users.txt -no-pass -dc-ip <dc> -format hashcat. Only svc-scanner is flagged DONT_REQ_PREAUTH.

Samba caveat: this DC is Samba, whose KDC demands pre-authentication for every account (GetNPUsers -no-pass returns KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED). The crackable AS-REP enc-part is emitted in any successful AS exchange, so retrieve svc-scanner's $krb5asrep$23$ hash with a native RC4-pinned pre-authenticated AS-REQ (see asrep.py in the image) rather than the no-pass roast.

The AS-REP is RC4 (etype 23): crack it with hashcat -m 18200 against a wordlist. The password is a weak word built from the scanner service's name and a year. Then: smbclient //dc/imaging -U 'LAKESIDE\svc-scanner%<cracked>' -c 'get flag.txt'.

steps.title: Name the technique
steps.prompt: What is the name of the attack that recovers a password offline from the Kerberos AS-REP of an account that does not require pre-authentication?

steps.title: Find the roastable account
steps.prompt: Which account has Kerberos pre-authentication disabled and is therefore AS-REP roastable? (username)

steps.title: Name the UAC flag
steps.prompt: Which userAccountControl flag, when set on an account, makes it AS-REP roastable? (its name)

steps.title: Name the ticket encryption
steps.prompt: Which encryption type is the AS-REP here, that makes it fast to crack? (name or Kerberos etype number)

steps.title: Pick the crack mode
steps.prompt: Which hashcat mode cracks an RC4 AS-REP ($krb5asrep$23$) hash?
